title: Sleeping on London Tube Platform Tracks
hook: 150,000 Londoners slept shoulder-to-shoulder on subway tracks.

scenes.text: When nightly Blitz bombing raids devastated London, 150,000 civilians took shelter seventy feet underground in the Tube network.
scenes.imagePrompt: 1940s London Underground curved tunnel station with white subway tiles and a wooden platform edge over steel train tracks. 2D flat cartoon illustration, thick dark outlines, warm muted palette, hand-painted textures, vertical 9:16, no people in the foreground, no text, no logos
scenes.voicedText: When nightly Blitz bombing raids devastated London, 150,000 civilians took shelter seventy feet underground in the Tube network.

scenes.text: At first, the government tried locking subway station gates, but desperate crowds bought penny tickets and simply refused to leave.

scenes.voicedText: At first, the government tried locking subway station gates, but desperate crowds bought penny tickets and simply refused to leave.

scenes.text: Families claimed their small patches of platform concrete each evening with blankets, tea thermoses, and cardboard suitcases.

scenes.text: Deep underground, entire communities formed: mobile tea trollies rolled down tracks, musical concerts played, and libraries lent books.

scenes.text: Conditions were stifling: the air was thick with disinfectant, and seven thousand trains rattled by on daytime schedules before night shutdowns.
